takeaway: Seven muscles attach the scapula to the chest wall; subclavius is not one of them. Serratus anterior paralysis (long thoracic nerve) causes winging.

question.text: Which of the following muscles is not attached to the scapula?
question.say: Which of the following muscles is not attached to the scapula?

lines.text: Here is the scapula, the friendly bone on the back, held by muscles on ropes.
Seven muscles attach the scapula to the chest wall. The two main ones are trapezius and serratus anterior.
The other five include levator scapulae, rhomboids, pectoralis minor and omohyoid. Each tied rope here has a green tick.
But look at the small muscle under the collarbone. Subclavius holds the clavicle and the first rib, far from the scapula, so its rope is cut.
One last point: paralysis of serratus anterior, supplied by the long thoracic nerve, gives a winged scapula.
So the muscle not attached to the scapula is subclavius.
